column1: Layer I: Phase 1 Foundation and Initial Intelligence
column2: Establish the central data foundation and deliver the first unified data access, AI query and NOC capabilities within 8 weeks.
Assess and connect GTPL KCBPL's existing applications, databases, monitoring platforms and reporting sources.

Inventories H8, 1IMS, Sathi Portal, NAS, NMS, PRTG, Zabbix, Cacti, WhatsApp, Nokia-related sources, DOT reports, NOC bandwidth sources and other discovered systems; confirms data owners, access methods, data availability and integration feasibility.
Establishes secure, reusable API, database and file-based connectors, with scheduled or on-demand ingestion where supported.
Integrates the sources agreed during discovery, prioritising customer, network and operational datasets required for the Lakehouse, initial AI query agent and NOC capabilities.
Validates the available Nokia data access arrangement, including the S3 and SSH-key approach mentioned in discussions; does not assume an API is available.
Assesses WhatsApp and other discovered sources for approved access, permissions and technical feasibility before committing to integration.
Tracks ingestion runs, records failures, supports retries where appropriate and exposes source-level integration status.
Creates a governed central foundation for customer, network and operational data.
Stores ingested source data in its received form with source identifiers, timestamps and batch or ingestion metadata for traceability.
Transforms and standardises agreed datasets into consistent structures suitable for authorised access, reporting and AI querying.
Applies agreed validation, cleansing and deduplication rules; records exceptions and data-quality issues for review.
Defines initial common data structures for the selected customer, network and operational datasets included in Phase 1.
Publishes validated and structured datasets for the unified interface, initial AI query agent and agreed NOC reporting.
Supports agreed scheduled or event-based refresh patterns according to each source's available access method and update frequency.
Maintains source and ingestion metadata so users and administrators can trace curated data back to its originating source where available.
Provides one controlled interface for authorised users to access available datasets and the initial AI query capability.
Provides an authenticated central interface to access the datasets and capabilities made available in Phase 1.

column1: Dataset catalogue and basic data views
column2: Lists available datasets and provides basic table or record views for authorised users.
Allows authorised users to search and filter supported datasets using available fields and permissions.
Displays basic charts or visual summaries for selected datasets where the data structure supports them.
Restricts platform and dataset access according to approved user roles and permissions.
Delivers one natural-language agent for querying selected, approved datasets through governed, read-only access.
Allows authorised users to ask supported questions in natural language about the selected Phase 1 datasets.
Retrieves information only from the approved datasets and within the requesting user's access permissions.
Generates answers and concise summaries based on retrieved data, with source or dataset context where available.

column1: Tables and basic charts in responses
column2: Presents query results as tables or basic visual summaries when appropriate and supported by the data.
Limits the initial agent to reading and analysing authorised data; it does not make production changes or execute write actions.
Identifies unsupported or ambiguous questions, requests clarification where needed and avoids presenting ungrounded answers.
Provides a consolidated monitoring view, basic alerts and selected bandwidth reporting for the agreed NOC sources.
Combines agreed monitoring information from PRTG, Zabbix and Cacti, subject to integration feasibility, into a single NOC view.
Displays selected availability, event and performance indicators made available by the integrated monitoring sources.
Raises basic alerts against agreed monitoring conditions or thresholds; advanced AI event correlation and autonomous remediation are excluded.
Produces selected bandwidth utilisation reports using agreed NOC monitoring data and reporting requirements.
Ensures controlled access, validation, operational readiness and a documented handover.
Enforces approved user roles and permissions across the platform, datasets and initial AI query capability.
Applies agreed security controls for data access, transfer and storage, based on the deployment model and GTPL KCBPL policies.
Records relevant user access, data operations and AI query activity for audit and troubleshooting, subject to the agreed design.
Confirms the required data-retention scope, including the one-year requirement raised in discussions, and validates on-premises, cloud or hybrid deployment constraints.
Validates ingestion, data quality, access permissions, AI query responses, NOC dashboard outputs, basic alerts and bandwidth reporting with GTPL stakeholders.
Provides agreed technical and user documentation, known limitations, operational handover and Phase 1 acceptance records.
